text:
emi: Quick notes from pairing in the policy editor sandbox. Found a few tiny UX/a11y pain points. Dropping them here so eng + design can triage. :clipboard:

samir: go for it, short bullets pls.

emi: 1) reorder affordance is easy to miss on touch; the handle only appears on hover. 2) sim panel spams detailed lines during active edits; makes it hard to keep context. 3) validation copy feels too technical and not action-oriented.

kelly: for copy, propose: "Conflict with earlier rule. View conflict" instead of compiler-y language. Short + click-to-action.

rachel: accessibility: suggest a keyboard grab mode: press G to enter grab mode, Enter to pick up, arrows to move, Enter to drop. Announce position changes like "Moved to 3 of 8" via role=status. Also ensure focus remains on the moved item.

samir: solid. Implementation note: add a CSS class .keyboard-drag and set aria-grabbed=true on the active element. Debounce simulation updates while the user is interacting (e.g., 600ms) to reduce noise.

emi: thanks. Also UX idea: collapse sim by default and show a concise header: "Matches: 14 | Conflicts: 2 | Samples: 6" with a chevron to expand. Clicking the Conflicts count filters the rules list to just conflicted rules.

morgan: +1. Could we also show a small "preview stale" badge when the list changes after running a preview? Helps avoid confusion if preview doesn't match current order.

kelly: copy variants I'll draft: friendly "This rule overlaps with an earlier rule. View overlap." neutral "Rule conflicts with earlier rule. View details." SR-only: "Conflict detected. Use View overlap to inspect."

opsbot: Sandbox run @2182468101: summary {matched:14, conflicts:2, samples:6} top_samples: [signup:9, api:3, cron:2]

rachel: contrast nit: the chevron and counts are ~3.0:1 on current bg. Need >=4.5:1 for body text. I'll add a figma note to darken the chip bg.

samir: action list: 1) add keyboard grab + aria announcements (me). 2) debounce sim updates while editing (me). 3) collapsed sim header + filter-on-pill (daniel?). 4) copy PR (kelly). 5) figma contrast tweak (rachel).

emi: i'll file the UX tickets and link them to policy-editor epic. small scope but should make reorder + preview far less confusing. Thanks y'all. :raised_hands:
